judged_text: create() no longer accepts or sends usernames, so the long-standing ability to add initial members at group-creation time is silently removed from the admin flow. Previously an admin could create a group and seed its membership in one step (createWithUsernames); now they must create the group, wait for it to persist, then add members separately — a user-facing workflow regression introduced by iteration without explicit acceptance of the capability removal.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly removes the ability to seed members during group creation: the admin controller `save` action no longer calls `createWithUsernames/saveWithUsernames` (now `group.create()` / `group.save()`), the `Discourse.Group#create`/`asJSON` payload no longer includes `usernames`, and the admin template only shows the add-members UI when `{{#if id}}` (i.e., after persistence). This is a workflow/feature regression, but it is an intentional behavior change reflected in both frontend and backend, not an accidental runtime defect shown by the diff itself.
